preamble: Five unpublished Bunthorne puzzles will appear posthumously between now and November.

clue.text: School mark approving funny business

parts.note: a tick is the mark a teacher puts by a correct answer

explanation.surface: A teacher's approving mark is awarded for some classroom clowning.
explanation.definitionFit: Schtick is a comedian's routine or gimmick, the funny business that is their trademark.

clue.text: As Phaedra's Hippolytus crushes underfoot

definitions.meaning: Hippolytus was the son of Theseus by an earlier wife, so Phaedra's son by marriage
read as two words, treads on

explanation.surface: In Greek myth Phaedra's stepchild tramples something.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippolytus was the son of Phaedra's husband Theseus by another woman; split in two the word means treads on.

clue.text: Great exemplar with all to do: watch for failing

indicators.note: failing suggests the words collapse and their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A model of greatness in a fuss, with a watch failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard act to follow is someone so outstanding that whoever comes next suffers by comparison: an exemplar.

clue.text: One taking Hood's place as playwright

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Sherwood Forest is the legendary home of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for Hood as dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood wrote plays with W H Auden as well as his Berlin novels.

clue.text: Knight, a prince of the Jewish community

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for knight
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A knight and a prince belong to the Jewish community.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V in the Henry IV plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Kahal is the Hebrew term for a congregation or organised Jewish community.

clue.text: Bismarck ruled this land of blue and Prince this land once red

definitions.text: Bismarck ruled this land of blue

parts.note: Russia was the heart of the Soviet Union, whose emblem and politics were Red

explanation.surface: Two countries contrasted by their historic colours and leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of blue' points to Prussian blue, the pigment, helping define the land Bismarck governed as Minister President.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was Minister President of the German kingdom of Prussia, which gave its name to the pigment Prussian blue.

clue.text: Smells coming from this river, right? Our tip erupted

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy

indicators.note: erupted suggests the letters burst out in a new order

explanation.surface: A river gives off smells, a rubbish tip having erupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for the fragrance it gives off.

clue.text: One true offspring: some mothers do 'ave 'em!

indicators.note: read as off-spring, the letters spring off into a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child is a true one, as the sitcom title has it.
explanation.walkthrough: Some Mothers Do 'Ave 'Em was a 1970s British sitcom; here it is read literally, since mothers have wombs.
explanation.definitionFit: The womb is the organ of pregnancy, so mothers (and other women) have one each.

clue.text: Long John Silver's expression in his aspen grove?

definitions.meaning: the pirate in Treasure Island exclaims this oath
aspens tremble in the wind, so a grove of them is shaking wood

explanation.surface: What a pirate says, transferred to a stand of quivering trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate's oath literally means 'make my wood quiver', which is what aspens' leaves do.

clue.text: Like the pain from Algerian gin almost

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A headache comes from drinking North African gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is a chest pain, and anginal describes something relating to it.

clue.text: Momentous thing, heart rate's disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of these three words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used here as a letter

explanation.surface: Something alarming has happened and someone's pulse is racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shattering is so significant it seems to shake the world, hence momentous.

clue.text: Aviation route switched in flight

indicators.note: switched says the two pieces trade places from the order the clue gives them

parts.note: ST, street, is a route through a town
air, as in air travel, stands for aviation

explanation.surface: An airline route has been changed while the plane is airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: one step is something found in a flight of steps, not an aircraft journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of individual steps, so each one is found in a flight.

clue.text: Indifferent to conversion of Caledonia

indicators.note: conversion means the letters of the old name for Scotland are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Scotland is lukewarm about any attempt to convert it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Laodiceans in Revelation were rebuked for being lukewarm, so the word means half-hearted or apathetic, particularly in religion.

clue.text: Trawlerman with a PC full of contacts?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, someone who works with nets, a fisherman

definitions.text: with a PC full of contacts?
definitions.meaning: someone who cultivates a large circle of useful acquaintances, perhaps over a computer link

explanation.surface: A fisherman owns a computer packed with names and addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the word is one who works nets; in modern usage it is one who builds professional contacts.

clue.text: In which calves take cover

parts.note: calves are the backs of the lower legs, not young cattle, and these long garments cover them

explanation.definitionFit: Long socks reaching up to just below the knee cover the calf muscles.

clue.text: Sri Lankan maiden trapped by shadow

indicators.note: trapped by says the single letter is held inside the follower word

parts.note: to shadow or tail someone is to follow them closely
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman from Sri Lanka is caught by someone following her.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of northern and eastern Sri Lanka and southern India.

clue.text: Bloodsucker in knitted twin-set? Run!

indicators.note: knitted means the doubled letters are worked into a new pattern
twin means two copies of the word

parts.note: the word as written
to fly is to run away

explanation.surface: A biting insect is found in a knitted cardigan set; escape!
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly of Africa feeds on blood and spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Lonely Lakeland water-bearer

parts.note: Wordsworth, poet of the English Lake District, wandered lonely as one of these, which carry rain

explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District (Lakeland) is a region of north-west England where Wordsworth lived; his best-known poem begins 'I wandered lonely as a ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds carry water vapour as rain, and Wordsworth's famous poem compares his loneliness to a drifting one.

clue.text: Pain in the heart nearly finished tutor

indicators.note: in says the pain sits inside the shortened heart
nearly finished means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: the core is the heart of something
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A tutor is nearly worn out, with heartache.
explanation.definitionFit: A coacher is one who coaches, a tutor or trainer.

clue.text: High point of some 9 recipe with ten ingredients

indicators.note: as ingredients, the letters of the two words are mixed together into a new dish

explanation.surface: A cooking recipe uses ten ingredients for a dramatic dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9-across, momentous: a seismic event has its focus at this point.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface above the focus of an earthquake, an earth-shattering event.

clue.text: What an enigmatist does, getting up to perform during scene change

indicators.note: during means one part goes in the middle of the other
change means the letters of the word are rearranged
in a down clue getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter rises to act in a scene change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scene change' reads like stage directions, but 'change' is the anagram signal on scene, and 'getting up' turns the verb for perform upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigmatist sets puzzles and riddles, putting messages in code.

clue.text: Liquidates a joint society

parts.note: a mortise is the slot of a mortise-and-tenon woodworking joint

explanation.surface: A shared organisation is being wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise a debt is to pay it off gradually, liquidating it.

clue.text: Substance of article on the setter

parts.note: the is the definite article
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The essence of a piece written by the compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme of a work is its subject matter or substance.

clue.text: Burst of speed put on by jet

definitions.meaning: an athlete puts on a sudden acceleration

explanation.surface: A runner speeds up, as if propelled by a jet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden increase in pace and a gush of liquid forced out.

clue.text: Total bill for one from the arboretum

parts.note: a sum is a total
AC, account, is a bill to be paid

explanation.surface: Someone tots up the bill for a tree from a botanical collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree, the kind of specimen grown in an arboretum.

clue.text: Endue child of all creation with "The Catcher in the Rye"

indicators.note: creation means a new thing is made from these letters

explanation.surface: Bestow on every child of creation a famous American novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the novel for its narrator: Salinger's teenage hero is himself the catcher in the rye of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrator of Salinger's novel imagines himself as the catcher in the rye who saves children, so the title names him.

clue.text: Immaturity of redhead?

parts.note: raw skin is red and sore
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Is having red hair a sign of being immature?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'redhead' as a ginger-haired person, but it splits into 'red' and 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawness is inexperience or greenness, the state of being immature.

clue.text: What Bacchus waved in years hence? Switch!

indicators.note: in, read after the swap, places the years inside the word for therefore
switch tells us to swap the order, reading years in hence

parts.note: thus and hence both mean therefore

explanation.surface: A question about what the god of wine waved in the years since, with an order to swap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch!' also hints at the definition, since the staff is a kind of switch or wand.
explanation.definitionFit: A thyrsus is the ivy-tipped staff carried by Bacchus and his followers in Greek myth.
